disease_label_per_paper: Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction with prolonged AKI after ABO-incompatible transfusion in an obstetric patient
presentation_summary: 29-year-old obstetric patient transferred with anuric AKI and intravascular hemolysis after receiving 100-200 mL from a blood unit before cesarean section.
Immediately after transfusion she developed flank and back pain, generalized aches, headache, fever, 1-1.5 L of bloody urine, then anuria.
On emergency department presentation three days later: BP 130/80, RR 20/min, HR 78/min, temperature 37.2 C, SpO2 96%, lower-extremity edema, and scleral jaundice.

Admission labs showed Hb 8.2 g/dL, WBC 14.2 x10^9/L, platelets 84 x10^9/L, creatinine 9.5 mg/dL, urea 166 mg/dL, LDH 800 U/L, total bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 1.4 mg/dL, pH 7.29, bicarbonate 11 mmol/L, and urine hemoglobin ++++.
The report states the transfusion unit was AB positive and the patient was A positive; that compatibility investigation is kept confirmatory/non-ranking.
